kind: Independent read-only same-contract workflow family reassessment, separate from apply approval and Astra audit
classification_reason: All material responsibilities in the two original frozen contracts now have verified shared Go support: typed equal-size old/new planning, source/preimage/complete-state guards, application and explicit revert, sorted bounded nonoverlapping edits, exclusive whole-copy writes, readback, whole-image containment and preserved registry ownership. Actual typed canonical JP restoration closes the former real typed-reversal gap; direct and CLI mixed slot/word reversals close the distinct coupled transaction proof gap. This conclusion uses the evidence together, not one label alone.

original_contracts.original_contract: Plan sorted bounded old/new byte edits once, retain preimages/idempotence/exclusive output/readback and registry ownership; no per-script writer. Recipes contain IDs, words, text and explicit old/new states. Existing Go plan/validateEdits/verifySource/patchCopy and Python stream_fix_run already own much of this.
Plan typed equal-size old/new edits, source guards, whole-copy application/revert and readback.

original_source_contract_details.guarded_transaction: Recipes contain IDs, words, text and explicit old/new states; no per-script writer; retain preimages/idempotence/exclusive output/readback and registry ownership.
original_source_contract_details.binary_edit: Plan typed equal-size old/new edits, source guards, whole-copy application/revert and readback. Recipe facts own addresses, explicit preimages, documented words, dependencies and bounded landing spans. Guards include complete before/new sets, partial-install refusal, alignment/overlap, original/shipping protection, source/hash and whole-image containment.
original_source_contract_details.baseline_scoring_rule: Full=all material responsibilities of the family have verified shared Go support with declarative inputs and preserved guards. Partial=some shared Go support exists but a material responsibility is missing/held. Unsupported=no verified Go workflow. Partial/unsupported earn zero completion credit; no invented0.5 scores or counts of duplicate historical scripts. Python references/tests may verify Go; operational Python remains an unmet Go responsibility.
